title: Why water boils at a lower temperature on mountains
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on mountains?
Why does pasta take longer to cook up high?
What temperature does water boil on Everest?

explain.say: At sea level water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Climb a mountain and it boils at a lower temperature, about 1 degree less for every 300 metres or so.

draw.text: Why water boils at a lower temperature on mountains

explain.say: Boiling happens when bubbles of steam can form inside the water. To do that, the steam must push back against the air pressing down on the water.
Higher up there is less air above you, so air pressure is lower. The bubbles need less push, so water boils at a lower temperature: about 84 degrees on top of Mont Blanc.
On Everest water boils at only about 70 degrees, too cool to cook pasta or eggs properly. Climbers use pressure cookers, which raise the pressure and the boiling point.

faq.q: Why does water boil at a lower temperature up high?
faq.a: There is less air pressing down on the water at altitude. Steam bubbles need less energy to form against that lower pressure, so water boils at a lower temperature.
asks: Why does altitude change boiling point?

faq.q: Why does pasta take longer to cook on a mountain?
faq.a: The water boils at a lower temperature, so even boiling water is cooler than it would be at sea level. Food cooks more slowly in cooler water.
asks: Why is cooking slower at high altitude?

faq.q: How does a pressure cooker help?
faq.a: A sealed pressure cooker traps steam, raising the pressure inside. That raises the boiling point to about 120 degrees Celsius, so food cooks faster.
asks: How does a pressure cooker work?

faq.q: Is boiling water on Everest hot enough to make tea?
faq.a: It boils at only about 70 degrees, so the tea is weak and lukewarm by normal standards, but it is still boiling.
asks: Can you make tea on Everest?

faq.q: What actually happens when water boils?
faq.a: Bubbles of water vapour form inside the liquid, not just at the top, because the vapour pushes as hard as the air pressing down. Then the temperature stops rising.

facts: Air pressure on the summit of Everest is about one third of the pressure at sea level.
A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water to about 120 degrees Celsius.
